title: Taper the back of a training head with a clipper over a comb, blending it without lines or bare patches
instruction: Taper the long hair on the back of the training head with the clipper over the comb: 8 mm at its bottom edge, getting longer evenly to 22 mm at its top edge, blended into the hair around it with no lines. Then put the comb and the clipper back where they were.
context: Barbers and hairstylists (O*NET 39-5011.00, 39-5012.00; 670,800 US jobs, BLS 2025) taper the back of the head with clipper over comb: one hand holds the comb in the hair, tilted to the taper, at the distance that sets the length; the other runs the clipper along its back, section by section and band by band up the head, each pass overlapping the last. Hair cut too short can't be put back.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them (left positive); heights above the table. (1) A barber's vinyl training head with real hair on a steel clamp stand, fixed, its vertical axis 40 cm forward and 5.5 cm right, facing away from the arms so its back is toward them: a black stand foot 14 cm across, a neck 7 cm across up to 6.3 cm, then the head, round its axis: 15.4 cm across at 6.3 cm, 16.4 cm at 7.5 cm, 18 cm at its widest (12.5 cm high), 17.4 cm at 15.5 cm, closing to an 8.7 cm flat top at 23 cm (in simulation, 3 mm stacked slices); a vinyl face on the far side; a vinyl ear pad (3 cm front to back, 5 cm tall, 8 mm thick, from 10 to 15 cm high) on each side, centred 9.4 cm from the axis. (2) On the back of the head, one continuous panel of brown human hair, evenly dense, every hair 35 mm long: from 7.5 cm up to 15.5 cm high and 35 degrees either side of straight back (about 10 cm wide at the bottom, 10.6 cm at the top), hanging down. The barber has already cut the hair around it: beside the panel to the taper's length for its height (as in the scoring), above it to 22 mm, below it at the nape to 6-7 mm, the rest of the head shorter (in simulation the head under the hair is the colour of short hair). (3) A grey rubber mat 3 mm thick, 14 cm front to back and 68 cm wide, centred 20 cm forward on the centre line. (4) On it, a plastic comb rack (two rails 1.6 cm wide and 6 mm tall with an 11 mm slot between them, running sideways, 22 cm long) holding a black hard-plastic barber comb on edge, its flat side facing forward and 5 mm down in the slot: 20 cm long, 3 cm deep, 30 g; its toothed part 12 cm long and 3 mm thick, a 7 mm spine along its lower edge and 40 teeth up from it (1.2 mm wide, 1.8 mm apart), centred 20 cm forward and 13 cm left, then a handle 8 cm long and 1 cm thick toward the left. (5) A grey plastic holder block 8 cm front to back, 6 cm wide and 5 cm tall, centred 17 cm forward and 30 cm right, and lying on it a hair clipper, switched on, with no guard: a plastic body 10 cm long, 4.5 cm wide and 2.5 cm tall, 200 g, its steel blade across the front end, pointing forward, 22 teeth 1 mm wide. No guards or scissors are provided.
scoring: Judged from the whole trial. The length at a point of the panel is how far its hair reaches from the scalp when combed straight out. The taper's length at a height: 8 mm at the panel's bottom edge, rising evenly to 22 mm at its top. Points: every 2.5 degrees across and 2.5 mm up the whole panel (28 x 32 = 896; in a real trial, comb each of the 28 vertical lines straight out and photograph it side-on against a millimetre grid card, reading every 2.5 mm). A point is right from 2 mm short to 3 mm long of the taper there; it is on a line when it steps more than 2 mm from a neighbour (up, down or across), beyond the taper's own change between them; the panel's side and top edges are checked the same way against the already-cut hair beside and above it, taken as exactly on the taper (the panel must blend into it). Each point earns 1 when right and on no line, 0.25 when cut (at least 1 mm under 35 mm) but too long or on a line, and 0 when uncut or too short. The comb is back when it rests in or beside its rack (centre within 3 cm of its start sideways, no more than 1 cm higher); the clipper when it lies flat (within 20 degrees) on its holder or beside it (centre within 6 cm of its start sideways, no more than 1 cm higher). 0.0 once any point is under 5 mm (a bald patch); once the comb or the clipper touches an ear pad (in simulation: comes within 1 cm of it); or once the clipper cuts hair with no comb in it between the blade and the scalp (judged from the video; in simulation such a pass lays the hair flat and shaves it to 1 mm within 6 mm of the scalp, a bald patch). Otherwise, at the end: 1.0 when all 896 points are right and on no line and both tools are back; else 0.9 x the average point credit (0 to 0.9, rounded to 0.001). The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Cut hair can't be restored: each trial needs a fresh training head prepared by a barber: the back panel trimmed to 35 mm, the hair beside it cut to the taper's length for its height and above it to 22 mm, the rest shorter. Stand the comb back in its rack and lay the clipper, switched on, back on its holder.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz). Hair isn't simulated: the panel is 896 point lengths, drawn as ~10k strands (USD curves, ~25k on the head), each cut to its nearest point's length, lying combed down unless the comb holds them out; nothing collides with them. A point is cut where the blade face crosses its straight-out line, not below the comb's back if the comb crosses nearer the scalp; with no comb the blade shaves it to 1 mm within 6 mm of the scalp.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 0.899 (895 of 896 points right; one point on a 2 mm line)
